nodes.title: Basic Terminology, Ligands & Denticity
points: Coordination entity: Central metal atom/ion bound to a fixed number of ions or molecules (ligands) enclosed in square brackets [ ].

Ligands (Lewis bases): Donors of electron pairs. Monodentate (Cl⁻, H₂O, NH₃, CN⁻); Bidentate (ethylenediamine 'en', oxalate 'ox²⁻', glycinate 'gly⁻'); Polydentate (EDTA⁴⁻ is hexadentate, 2 N and 4 O donors).
Ambidentate ligands: Monodentate ligands having two different donor atoms: NO₂⁻ (nitro -N or nitrito -O); SCN⁻ (thiocyanato -S or isothiocyanato -N).
Chelate effect: Chelating ligands (bidentate/polydentate forming ring complexes) provide exceptional thermodynamic stability over monodentate ligands due to positive entropy change (ΔS° > 0).

formulas.label: EDTA⁴⁻ hexadentate donor atoms
formulas.expr: EDTA⁴⁻ coordinates via 2 nitrogen and 4 oxygen atoms (forms 5 stable chelate rings)

formulas.label: Chelate effect thermodynamic relation
formulas.expr: ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS° (chelation increases free particles in solution, ΔS° > 0)

nodes.title: Werner's Theory & Effective Atomic Number (EAN)
points: Werner's postulates: Central metal possesses two types of valency: Primary (ionizable, non-directional, satisfied by negative ions = oxidation state) and Secondary (non-ionizable, directional = coordination number).
Cobalt ammine precipitation with excess AgNO₃: [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ gives 3 AgCl↓; [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ gives 2 AgCl↓; [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl gives 1 AgCl↓; [Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃] gives 0 AgCl↓ (non-electrolyte).
Effective Atomic Number (EAN): EAN = Z − (Oxidation State) + 2 × (Coordination Number). If EAN equals atomic number of next noble gas (36 Kr, 54 Xe, 86 Rn), complex shows enhanced stability.

nodes.title: IUPAC Nomenclature of Coordination Complexes
points: Naming order: Cation named before anion. Ligands named in alphabetical order before central metal.
Ligand endings: Anionic ligands end in '-o' (chlorido, cyanido, oxalato, sulfato, nitrito); Neutral ligands: H₂O (aqua), NH₃ (ammine), CO (carbonyl), en (ethane-1,2-diamine).
Prefixes: di, tri, tetra; or bis, tris, tetrakis for polydentate ligands or names containing numerical prefixes.

Metal name ending: In cationic/neutral complex, standard metal name is used; In anionic complex, metal ends in '-ate' (ferrate, cuprate, argentate, cobaltate, platinate). Oxidation state written in Roman numerals in parentheses.

nodes.title: Structural Isomerism in Coordination Compounds
points: Ionization isomerism: Exchange of ligands between coordination sphere and ionization sphere (e.g. [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br gives pale yellow ppt with AgNO₃; [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ gives white ppt with BaCl₂).
Hydrate / Solvate isomerism: Exchange of water molecules inside and outside sphere (e.g. [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ violet; [Cr(H₂O)₅Cl]Cl₂·H₂O blue-green; [Cr(H₂O)₄Cl₂]Cl·2H₂O dark green).
Linkage isomerism: Occurs with ambidentate ligands (e.g. [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ yellow nitro-N vs [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]Cl₂ red nitrito-O).
Coordination isomerism: Interchange of ligands between cationic and anionic coordination entities (e.g. [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆] and [Cr(NH₃)₆][Co(CN)₆]).

nodes.title: Stereoisomerism: Geometrical & Optical Isomerism
points: Geometrical isomerism (cis/trans): In square planar complexes [Ma₂b₂] (e.g. cis-[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] cisplatin is anticancer, trans is inactive); [Mabcd] gives 3 isomers. Note: [Ma₄] and [Ma₃b] do NOT show GI.
Octahedral geometrical isomers: [Ma₄b₂] shows cis and trans; [Ma₃b₃] shows facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomers.
Optical isomerism (Enantiomers): Requires non-superimposable mirror image and absence of plane of symmetry. [M(AA)₃] (e.g. [Co(en)₃]³⁺) shows d- and l-enantiomers.
cis vs trans-[M(AA)₂b₂] chirality: cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ is chiral and optically active; trans-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ has a plane of symmetry, hence is achiral and optically INACTIVE.

formulas.label: Facial (fac) and Meridional (mer) isomers
formulas.expr: [Co(NH₃)₃(NO₂)₃]: fac (triangular face) vs mer (plane containing center)

formulas.label: Optical activity of [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ isomers
formulas.expr: cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ = Optically active (chiral) | trans-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ = Optically inactive (achiral, plane of symmetry)

nodes.title: Valence Bond Theory (VBT) & Magnetic Properties
points: VBT concept: Hybridization of metal orbitals with donation of electron pairs from ligands. Coordination number 4: sp³ (tetrahedral) or dsp² (square planar). Coordination number 6: d²sp³ (inner orbital) or sp³d² (outer orbital).
Inner orbital complex (d²sp³, low spin): Uses inner (n−1)d orbitals; strong field ligands cause pairing of d-electrons (e.g. [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺).
Outer orbital complex (sp³d², high spin): Uses outer nd orbitals; weak field ligands do not cause pairing (e.g. [FeF₆]³⁻, [CoF₆]³⁻).

Square planar vs Tetrahedral Nickel: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ has strong field CN⁻ → d-electrons pair up → dsp² (square planar, diamagnetic); [NiCl₄]²⁻ has weak field Cl⁻ → sp³ (tetrahedral, paramagnetic, 2 unpaired e⁻).

formulas.label: Hybridization and geometry correlation
formulas.expr: sp³ = Tetrahedral | dsp² = Square planar | d²sp³ = Inner octahedral | sp³d² = Outer octahedral

formulas.label: Nickel coordination complexes comparison
formulas.expr: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻: dsp² (Square planar, diamagnetic, μ=0) | [NiCl₄]²⁻: sp³ (Tetrahedral, paramagnetic, μ=2.83 BM)

nodes.title: Crystal Field Theory (CFT): Splitting & Spectrochemical Series
points: CFT concept: Degenerate d-orbitals split in electrostatic field of ligands. In octahedral field, d(x²-y²) and d(z²) point along axes → raised to e_g (+0.6 Δ₀); d(xy), d(yz), d(zx) point between axes → lowered to t₂g (−0.4 Δ₀).
Tetrahedral splitting (Δ_t): Inverted splitting (e lower, t₂ higher). Δ_t = (4/9) Δ₀. Since Δ_t < P (pairing energy), tetrahedral complexes are ALWAYS high-spin (no pairing).
Octahedral high spin vs low spin: If Δ₀ > P (strong field): electrons pair in t₂g (low-spin); If Δ₀ < P (weak field): electrons enter e_g before pairing (high-spin).
Spectrochemical Series (increasing ligand field strength): I⁻ < Br⁻ < S²⁻ < SCN⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O < NCS⁻ < EDTA⁴⁻ < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO.

formulas.label: Octahedral CFSE formula
formulas.expr: CFSE = [−0.4 × n(t₂g) + 0.6 × n(eg)] Δ₀ + mP (where P = pairing energy)

formulas.label: Spectrochemical series order
formulas.expr: I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO (CO is strongest field ligand)

nodes.title: Stability, Color & Applications of Coordination Compounds
points: Stability of complexes: Measured by overall stability constant β_n = K₁ × K₂ × ... × K_n. Greater β_n indicates greater thermodynamic stability.
Origin of color: d-d transitions. Electron promoted from t₂g to e_g level by absorbing visible light; transmitted complementary color is observed.
Metallurgical applications: Extraction of gold and silver by cyanide leaching ([Au(CN)₂]⁻, [Ag(CN)₂]⁻); Mond's process for refining nickel via volatile [Ni(CO)₄].
Biological & Medicinal applications: Chlorophyll (Mg complex), Hemoglobin (Fe²⁺ complex), Vitamin B₁₂ (Co complex); Cisplatin [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] in cancer treatment; EDTA for lead poisoning.

formulas.label: Overall stability constant relation
formulas.expr: β_n = K₁ × K₂ × ... × K_n; log β_n = log K₁ + log K₂ + ... + log K_n

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Derivations
points: Board Q1: State Werner's coordination theory postulates and deduce secondary valencies from AgNO₃ precipitation data.
Board Q2: Calculate EAN of [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, and [Ni(CO)₄] (all equal 36, obeying EAN rule).
Board Q3: Explain why [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is diamagnetic and square planar, while [NiCl₄]²⁻ is paramagnetic and tetrahedral using VBT.
Board Q4: Draw structures of cis- and trans-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ and state which isomer is optically active and why (cis has no plane of symmetry, trans has plane of symmetry).

nodes.title: MHT-CET High-Speed Shortcuts & Exception Traps
points: TRAP 1: Optical activity shortcut: trans-[M(AA)₂b₂] is ALWAYS optically inactive (plane of symmetry). cis-[M(AA)₂b₂] and [M(AA)₃] are ALWAYS optically active (chiral).
TRAP 2: Tetrahedral complexes NEVER form low-spin complexes because Δ_t is always less than pairing energy P (Δ_t = 4/9 Δ₀).
TRAP 3: Geometrical isomerism in square planar complexes: [Ma₄], [Ma₃b], [Mab₃] show 0 GI. [Ma₂b₂] shows 2 (cis/trans); [Ma₂bc] shows 2; [Mabcd] shows 3 isomers.
TRAP 4: Number of ions produced in solution: Count counter ions + the 1 coordination entity bracket. Example: K₃[Fe(CN)₆] produces 3 K⁺ + 1 [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ = 4 ions (van 't Hoff factor i = 4).
TRAP 5: Strong field ligands (C, N donors): CO, CN⁻, en, NH₃ cause electron pairing. Weak field ligands (halogens, O, S donors): F⁻, Cl⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, H₂O, OH⁻ do not cause pairing.

formulas.label: Van 't Hoff factor (i) for complete ionization
formulas.expr: i = total number of ions produced per formula unit (e.g. [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ → i = 3)
